title: Over-claim: 'no sampling-based method' only rules out i.i.d. Bernoulli; current file is a further (sampling) regression

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Over-claim in the current `solution.tex`: "No sampling-based method can settle the general case."**

The current live `solution.tex` is the **matrix-Chernoff sampling** version (distinct from the KS_r-reduction file described in q6-23 — this is a *further* regression). It contains a section titled *"No sampling-based method can settle the general case"* whose Proposition only proves a $\sqrt N$ loss for **i.i.d. Bernoulli vertex inclusion** on $C_N$:

$$\Pr[S\text{ is }\varepsilon\text{-light}]\le e^{-p^2\lfloor N/2\rfloor}\ \Rightarrow\ \mathbb E|S|=pN=O(\sqrt N).$$

This computation is **correct** for that one scheme, but the section's title and the "Remaining ingredient" framing ("must be supplied by a deterministic interlacing/barrier argument rather than by sampling") **over-generalize** it to *all* sampling/randomized methods. The proposition rules out only independent Bernoulli inclusion; it says nothing about dependent random selection, pipage rounding, or interlacing-family (MSS-style) arguments — and, crucially, it does not establish that the **deterministic greedy top-σ barrier** proof (previously verified complete with $c=1/42$; see q6-23) is the *only* route.

**Why this matters (faithfulness / no-retreat).** The framing presents the universal-constant question as essentially open pending a "new deterministic interlacing-type argument," whereas a complete deterministic barrier proof was already in the issue history. A solver reading the current file may wrongly conclude the problem is unresolved.

**Requested fix.** Either (i) restore the verified deterministic greedy top-σ barrier proof (recommended; it directly answers YES with $c=1/42$ for all $G$, all $\varepsilon$, including cliques/expanders), or (ii) if keeping the sampling document, retitle the section to "i.i.d. Bernoulli sampling loses a polynomial factor" and remove the unsupported claim that *no* sampling-based method can work.

Note: the technical lemmas of the current file are individually correct — I symbolically verified the matrix-Chernoff form $d(e\mu/t)^{t/R}$ equals Tropp's standard bound times $e^{\mu/R}\ge1$ (valid looser bound), and numerically verified the decoupling $X\preceq Y$ on $K_5$. The defect is the over-claim and the partiality, not a false sub-lemma.
